   135.25 GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE.
   (a)   The purpose of this section is to provide employees of the Division of
Police an opportunity for discussion of any request or complaint, other than
disciplinary matters, and to establish a procedure to allow such complaint to
be heard in the event an employee first chooses to discuss the matter with his
or her supervisors and the administration with hopes of settling same. All of
the employees of the Division of Police shall select from among the Department
employees three representatives on March 1, 1989, and annually each year
thereafter to form the Division of Police Department Committee. All grievances
must be handled in the following manner:
   Step 1: Any employee who believes he or she has a complaint may present a
brief written complaint to and discuss such complaint with his or her immediate
supervisor and with a member of the department committee present, if so
desired, in an attempt to settle the complaint. For the purposes of this
section, a day shall mean a business day and not a calendar day. Such informal
meeting or discussion shall be conducted within five days from the date such
written complaint is received by the supervisor above specified. The supervisor
shall respond in writing to the complaint within five days from the date of the
informal meeting or discussion held to discuss the complaint therein suggesting
complaint resolution.
   (b)   In the event any action taken as a result of Step 1 above fails to
resolve the complaint to the satisfaction of the complaining party, such
employee may refer the matter to Step 2 procedures:
   Step 2: In order for a complaint to be considered further, an employee must
notify in writing the Chief of the Department or his/her designee that he or
she desires to discuss the matter with them in an attempt to settle the matter.
   (c)   The Chief or his/her designee shall schedule an informal meeting or
discussion date within five days from the date such written complaint is
received. At such informal meeting or discussion, the employee will be
permitted to have present a member of the Division of Police. The Chief or his/
her designee shall respond in writing to the complaint within seven days from
the date of the informal meeting or discussion held to discuss the complaint
therein suggesting complaint resolution.
   (d)   In the event any action taken as a result of Step 2 above fails to
resolve the complaint to the satisfaction of the complaining party, such
employee may follow the procedure set forth in Step 3:
   Step 3: A complaint appeal to the Mayor pursuant to this Step 3 procedure
must be made in writing and the writing must state the nature of the complaint.
The Mayor or his designated representative shall schedule a meeting with the
employee, a member of the Division of Police for the purpose of reviewing and
discussing the complaint within seven days from the date such written complaint
is received. The Mayor shall respond in writing to the complaint within seven
days from the date of the meeting therein suggesting complaint resolution. The
ruling of the Mayor shall be final.
   (e)   The following of this grievance procedure shall not cause a
complaining employee to be barred from Civil Service Commission procedures due
to the passage of time while the complaint is considered in the manner set
forth in Steps 1, 2 or 3 above in the event the matter is within the
jurisdiction of the Civil Service Commission. Nothing contained in the
grievance procedure shall be construed to apply to disciplinary actions which
are otherwise appealable to the Civil Service Commission.
(Ord. 2004-199. Passed 12-21-04.)
   135.26 ADDITIONAL BENEFITS.
   (a)   Vacation. Employees shall be eligible for vacation leave with pay
after one year of service with the City. Vacation time shall be earned annually
as follows:
 
After one year continuous service:         two weeks
After six years’ continuous service:     three weeks
After twelve years’ continuous service:  four weeks
After seventeen years’ continuous servicefive weeks
   The City will permit up to two weeks of vacation to be taken one day at a
time with advanced written permission of the Police Chief or his designee.
   Vacation time must be used prior to December 31 of the year in which it is
earned. After the first twelve months of service, vacation leave shall accrue
on a calendar (January 1 to December 31) basis. No more than one officer per
shift shall be allowed off for vacation at any one time. In case of emergency
or unusual circumstances requiring an officer to work during his/her vacation
period, the officer shall receive compensation for the time he/she would have
had a vacation, if recommended by the Police Chief and approved by City
Council.
   For purposes of this subsection, length of service shall be determined by
the date of hire or date of appointment or election and qualification for
office of each employee. No vacation credit shall be given to any employee
hired by the City who has previously accumulated vacation time due from another
public employer.
   Each January, each employee, in order of seniority, shall specify on a list
provided by the City the weeks (maximum of two weeks) he/she desires to take
off for vacation. Separate vacation lists shall be provided for each shift. No
more than one employee per shift shall be allowed off for vacation at any one
time. After all employees have been provided the opportunity to select their
initial two week vacation period, those employees entitled to additional weeks
of vacation shall choose, one week at a time, from the available weeks
remaining on the vacation list for his/her shift. Such procedure shall be
followed until all employees have exhausted their vacation entitlement.
Employees may hold a maximum of one week of vacation per year to be split into
single days. All selections must be made prior to January 31 of each year. As
indicated, vacations, insofar as practicable, will be granted according to
employee requests. However, the Chief shall have exclusive authority to allot
vacation periods and to change such allotments.
   Employees shall be permitted to “split” one week of vacation with prior
approval of the Police Chief.
   (b)   Longevity Compensation. All full-time employees of the Police
Department, including the Police Chief, who have attained the years of
continuous service indicated in the following table in any calendar year, shall
be entitled to longevity compensation as follows:
Years of Service               Percentage
First through third            0
Fourth and fifth               2
Sixth and seventh              2-1/2
Eighth and ninth               3
Tenth and eleventh             3-1/2
Twelfth and thirteenth         4
Fourteenth and fifteenth       4-1/2
Sixteenth and seventeenth      5
Eighteenth and nineteenth      5-1/2
Twenty and twenty-first        6
Twenty-second and twenty-third 6-1/2
Twenty-fourth and over         7
   All other years of continuous service and percentages will remain the same.
The maximum amount to be paid to any Commander of the Police Department shall
be three thousand seven hundred dollars ($3,700.00) effective January 1, 2005.
There shall be no maximum limitation for the Chief of Police. This adjustment
shall be based on an employee’s original date of hire or appointment and shall
be applied to an employee’s first full pay period following his/her anniversary
date of employment. No pay other than base pay shall be adjusted for longevity.

(Ord. 2004-199. Passed 12-21-04.)
   (c)   Group Insurance Program.  The City will make available group insurance
benefits provided through United Health Care, or equivalent benefits provided
by another carrier. In addition, the City will make available group insurance
benefits for single and family coverage provided through Kaiser Permanente HMO.
Effective October 1, 2001, all employees shall contribute eight percent (8%) of
the premium for family health insurance and eight percent (8%) of the premium
for single health insurance, provided that an employee’s contribution shall not
exceed forty-five dollars ($45.00) per month. The City shall create a Section
125 plan, which will permit the City to make the contributions on a pre-tax
basis.
   Newly-hired employees will be provided group insurance benefits upon
completion of their insurance enrollment period or a period of three (3) months
of continuous active service, whichever comes first.
   The City will provide to all eligible employees the Health Care Benefit
Plans, Dental Insurance (MetLife Dental or benefits of the same overall level
or greater provided by another carrier) and Vision Care benefits with
contributions as noted above, including a twenty dollar ($20.00) deductible
prescription drug plan. If generic drugs or a prescription maintenance plan is
used, the deductible will be ten dollars ($10.00). The prescription drug plan
deductible for Kaiser Permanente plan is ten dollars ($10.00).
(Ord. 2005-078. Passed 5-3-05.)
   (d)   Compensation Time Bank. All employees, except the Chief of Police, may
choose to receive all overtime in either compensation or compensatory time at
the time the overtime is worked. An employee may accumulate compensatory time
up to 200 straight-time hours, at which point all overtime shall be paid as
earned. However, an employee may buy back accumulated compensatory time at any
time by advising the Police Chief in writing. When compensatory time is paid,
it shall be calculated from the employee’s base rate at the time it is earned.
   Compensation time banked hours will be at the option of the employee. All
overtime worked after employee’s compensation time bank reaches 200 hours must
be paid in cash in compliance with the provisions of Section
157.19, “Overtime Compensation”, of the Codified Ordinances and the Fair Labor
Standards Act.
   (e)   Sick Leave. Effective January 1, 1989, all officers, sergeants and
lieutenants and including commanders in the Division of Police, with the
exception of the Chief of Police, who shall be subject to Section
157.11, shall be entitled to sick leave of three and one-tenths hours for each
completed eighty hours of service. Employees may use sick leave, upon approval
of the Police Chief or his designee, for absence due to illness, injury,
exposure to a contagious disease which could be communicated to other
employees, and illness or death in the employee's immediate family. Unused sick
leave shall be cumulative without limit for a maximum period of twenty-five
years for sick leave purposes or payment at the time of retirement as set forth
herein.
      (1)   For the purposes of this section, the words "immediate family"
shall be construed to mean and be limited to the parents, spouse, children,
brothers, sisters, grandparents, mother-in-law or father-in-law of the
employee.
      (2)   When sick leave is used, it shall be deducted from employee's
credit on the basis of one hour for every one hour of absence from previously
scheduled work.
      (3)   Permanent employees who render part-time service shall be entitled
to sick leave for the full time actually worked at the same rate as that
granted to full-time employees. Seasonal, intermittent, per diem or hourly
employees shall not be entitled to sick leave.
      (4)   The Police Chief or his designee shall require the employee to
furnish a qualified affidavit that his absence was caused by illness due to any
of the causes mentioned in this section, if such absence was in excess of three
days, or for a lesser period of time, if the Chief or his designee feels that
such affidavit is necessary to prevent abuse of the provisions of this section.
      (5)   The City reserves the right to require each employee applying for
sick leave to be examined by a doctor named by the City to ascertain the nature
and extent of illness claimed.
      (6)   Each employee with ten or more years of service shall be entitled
to withdraw pay from their accumulated sick time at any period prior to their
retirement, provided their request for early withdrawal is made in writing to
the Director of Finance in January of each year on a form provided by the City.
The maximum withdrawal is ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per year by an
eligible employee. Additional withdrawals may be approved by the Director of
Finance.
      (7)   Early withdrawal compensation of sick time will be computed on the
basis of an employee's hourly rate of pay at the time of hire, combined with
the hourly rate of pay at the time of his or her withdrawal, divided by two and
multiplied by his/her accumulated sick hours being withdrawn at the time.
      (8)   Employees who have acquired ten or more years of service at the
time of separation (i.e., retirement, layoff, death, dismissal or resignation)
shall receive pay for unused sick leave based upon their hourly rate of pay at
the time in which they were hired combined with the hourly rate of pay at their
retirement divided by two and multiplied by his or her accumulated sick time
hours. Such payment shall be made only once to an employee.
      (9)   For the purpose of such payment, the maximum permitted accumulation
of unused sick time shall not exceed twenty-five years of service from an
employee's anniversary date of hire. However, an employee retained in the
employment of the City after twenty-five years of service shall be permitted to
accumulate sick time hours solely for the purpose of sick leave in any given
year thereafter.
      (10)   For purposes of compensation under this provision, hourly rate of
pay shall be defined as an employee's actual base rate excluding all other wage
tied benefits.
      (11)   Employees abusing this section are subject to discipline, up to
and including discharge.
   (f)   Compensation at the Time of Resignation, Dismissal, Retirement, Layoff
or Death. If any employee is eligible to receive vacation, holiday, longevity,
compensatory time, accumulated sick leave and any other pay normally received
in the course of employment which also includes pro rata pay due for the
current year at the current rate of pay in accordance with the applicable
provisions of the ordinances of the City, said compensation shall be paid to
the employee or in the event of death, to the employee's estate.
   (g)   Funeral Leave. When death occurs in the immediate family of an
employee, i.e., legal spouse, mother, father, mother-in-law, father-in-law,
son, daughter, brother, sister and grandparents, an employee, upon request,
will be excused for up to three consecutive scheduled days which include the
day of the funeral (or for such fewer days as the employee may be absent),
provided the employee attends the funeral service. Such payment will be at the
employee’s normal rate.
   If additional time is needed, the employee, upon request and approval, may
apply sick days unless circumstances preclude such application at which time
the employee and Police Chief may agree to another method.
   (h)   Sick Leave Credit. When a Commander in the Division of Police does not
use sick time for a continuous period of six months, eight hours of straight
time compensation shall be credited to that supervisor’s compensation time bank
for the year 2003 and thereafter. No more than sixteen hours straight time
shall be credited to the supervisor’s compensation time bank for the year 2003
and thereafter.
   (i)   Holidays. All police officers, including Commanders, shall be entitled
to eleven (11) paid holidays (88 hours) and two (2) paid personal days per
calendar year as approved by the Chief of Police. No police officer shall be
entitled to time off on a City, state or Federal holiday unless such time is
requested and approved by the Chief of Police, providing the request is
submitted no later than forty-eight (48) hours before the commencement of the
holiday (except in case of emergency as determined by the Police Chief or his
or her designee). Should a police officer actually work on an actual holiday,
he or she shall receive compensation for the hours worked at the rate of one
and one-half times his or her regular rate of pay, or in lieu thereof, he or
she may choose to receive compensatory time under subsection (d) hereof.
   (j)   Pension. The City will make a contribution to the Police and Fire
Pension Fund of nineteen and one-half percent (19-1/2%) or as required by State
law.
   (k)   Infectious Disease. The City will provide required medical attention,
including inoculations, for employees or family members who either contract
infectious disease or may be exposed to infectious disease which arises
directly out of the work environment.
   (l)   Military Leave. Employees shall be granted leaves of absence for
military duty in accordance with federal and state law. In the case of a
declared war, the City shall pay the difference between the employee’s pay with
the City and his or her military pay.
   (m)   Jury Duty. An employee, while serving upon a jury in any court of
record, shall be paid at his regular salary rate for each of his work days
during the period of time so served.
   (n)   Unpaid Personal Leave. Leaves of absence for good reasons without pay
may be granted at the sole discretion of the Chief and the Mayor/Director of
Public Safety.
   (o)   Reimbursement of Training Expenses. If an employee voluntarily
terminates his employment with the City within one year from initial date of
employment, the employee will reimburse the City for the cost of the City of
all basic and special training, educational courses of study, seminars and any
other related special educational programs as well as related costs, including
travel expenses, provided to the employee at the expense of the City.
      (1)   Any new training, schooling, classification or position will be
offered to all existing members before any new members are hired for said
purpose.
      (2)   The City shall pay for schooling and/or training if approved by the
Police Chief.
   (p)   Training. All mandatory training, excluding travel time to and from
school, shall be considered time worked.
      (1)   All voluntary training and off-premises classroom education,
including related field work, which has been approved by the Chief of Police or
his designee shall be paid either in compensatory time or overtime only at the
base rate. (Employees are not to be compensated for non-classroom study time.)
      (2)   All travel time to and from training, whether voluntary or
mandatory, shall be paid either in compensatory time only at the base rate,
unless an employee has accumulated 100 straight-time hours of compensatory
time, at which time said training shall be paid in compensation at the base
rate.
      (3)   Officers who are designated and assigned as Field Training Officers
(FTOS) shall be paid one hour’s pay for each shift spent in training or
retraining employees.
   (q)   Court Time. Police employees, when required to appear in Bedford
Municipal Court at a time when the beginning and end of the appearance is
wholly during off-duty hours, shall be paid for the actual time spent in
attendance at such court (including reasonable travel time) at a minimum of
three hours of regular base pay or overtime, whichever is appropriate.
Employees required to appear in any other courts shall be paid for the actual
time spent in attendance at court or a minimum of four hours. In the event that
an employee is required to report to duty earlier than normally scheduled in
order to appear in court, following when he commences his normal shift of duty,
or is required to remain on duty after his normal shift of duty, or is required
to remain on duty after his normal quitting time to complete a court appearance
which begins while on duty, he shall be treated as being on overtime during
those extra hours, instead of the foregoing minimums. No person shall be
entitled to payment under this section unless required to appear in court by
the directive of a superior or by a directive of the Department of Law, or by
subpoena legally issued and served in a case in which the City is a party to
the action, either directly or as the arresting entity in a criminal action
prosecuted in the name of the State of Ohio.
   Employees who are required to use their personal vehicle to travel to and
from the police station to court shall receive mileage at the rate established
by the City.
   (r)   Call-in Time. Police employees, when required to report to work other
than for court or training evolutions not contiguous to regular scheduled shift
time, shall be paid for actual time worked or a minimum of four hours of
compensatory time.
   (s)   Damage to Property and Vehicles. Employees entrusted with City
vehicles or property who, through their own negligence, damage such vehicles or
property shall be subject to disciplinary actions.
(Ord. 2004-199. Passed 12-21-04.)
   135.261 SENIORITY.
   (a)   Seniority for a full-time employee shall be that employee’s length of
continuous service with the City. For the purpose of calculating length of
service, the date of an employee’s service shall be counted from his most
recent date of hire. An employee shall have no seniority during his
probationary period but, upon completion of the probationary period, seniority
shall be retroactive to the date of hire.
   (b)   Seniority shall be broken when an employee:
      (1)   Quits or resigns;
      (2)   Is discharged for cause;
      (3)   Is laid off more than one year;
      (4)   Is absent without notice for five consecutive duty days;
      (5)   Fails to report for work when recalled from layoff within three
work days from the date on which the City sends or delivers the employee notice
by certified mail (return receipt requested) (to such employee’s last known
address as shown on the City’s records).
   (c)   For the term of this agreement, in the case of a personnel reduction,
the employee with the least seniority, regardless of classification or
position, shall be laid off first. Employees shall be recalled in order of
their seniority, regardless of their classification or position. No new
employee shall be hired until laid-off employees have been given ample
opportunity to return to work.
(Ord. 2004-199. Passed 12-21-04.)
   135.27 CONTRACTS AUTHORIZED BY COUNCIL.
   Should any of the employees of the Division of Police enter into an
Agreement authorized by Council concerning economic conditions and benefits,
the terms of the Agreement shall control the economic conditions and benefits
of such employees and any conflicting provision of this chapter shall be
subject to the terms of the Agreement for the covered employees.
(Ord. 2004-199. Passed 12-21-04.)
   135.28 ASSISTANT POLICE CHIEF  SHALL SERVE AS CORRECTIONS ADMINISTRATOR.
   (a)   The Assistant Chief of the Police Department shall serve in the
capacity of Corrections Administrator.
   (b)   The Assistant Chief shall have or acquire within one (1) year of the
date of appointment and maintain the following qualifications as a condition of
employment.
   State of Ohio Corrections Officer certification.
(Ord. 2012-48. Passed 3-20-12.)
   135.29 CORRECTIONS FACILITY SECRETARY .
   (a)   There is hereby established within the Division of Police the position
of full-time Corrections Facility Secretary who shall be under the immediate
control and supervision of the Assistant Chief and be appointed by the Mayor.
The position of Secretary shall be within the unclassified service.
   (b)   The Secretary shall be at least eighteen (18) years of age and a high
school graduate or possess equivalent experience and/or relevant education and
shall perform such duties as are set forth in the City’s Employee Job
Descriptions and as the same are hereafter amended and approved by the Mayor/
Director of Public Safety, the Police Chief and the Assistant Chief. The
Secretary shall receive such compensation as authorized by Council and shall
receive such benefits as indicated under Chapter
157, Employees Generally.
   (c)   The Secretary shall have and maintain the following qualifications as
a condition of employment:
At least one (1) year of clerical experience, or the equivalent combination of
training and/or experience.
      (Ord. 2012-48. Passed 3-20-12.)
   135.30 CORRECTIONS FACILITIES COOKS.
   (a)   There are hereby established within the Division of Police the
positions of two (2) full-time and four (4) part-time cooks, who shall be under
the immediate control and supervision of the Assistant Chief, to be appointed
by the Mayor. The positions of full-time and part-time cooks shall be within
the unclassified service. The terms of an Agreement authorized by Council
concerning economic conditions and benefits shall control the economic and
conditions and benefits of such employees. Otherwise, such employees shall
receive such benefits as indicated under Chapter
157, Employees Generally.
   (b)   The two (2) full-time cooks shall have and perform the following
duties:
      (1)   The full-time cook shall be responsible for duties associated with,
but not limited to, the operations of the City Jail Kitchen as are set forth in
the City’s Employee Job Descriptions and as the same are hereafter amended and
approved by the Mayor/Director of Public Safety, the Police Chief and Assistant
Chief.
      (2)   An applicant for the position of full-time cook shall be at least
eighteen (18) years of age and a high school graduate or possess equivalent
experience and/or relevant education and have experience in the preparation of
meals for groups of people, and knowledge of sanitation and food preparation as
prescribed by the Health Department.
   (c)   The four (4) part-time cooks shall not exceed a total of ninety-six
(96) hours per week and shall have and perform the following duties:
      (1)   The part-time cook shall be responsible for duties associated with,
but not limited to, the operations of the City Jail Kitchen as are set forth in
the City’s Employee Job Descriptions and as the same are hereafter amended and
approved by the Mayor/Director of Public Safety, the Police Chief and Assistant
Chief.
      (2)   No individual part-time cook shall work more than thirty-two (32)
hours per week providing coverage for the kitchen as required to operate the
facility, according to the Minimum Standards for Jails in Ohio.
      (3)   An applicant for the position of part-time cook shall have
experience in the preparation of meals for groups of people, and knowledge of
sanitation and food preparation as prescribed by the Health Department.
         (Ord. 2012-48. Passed 3-20-12.)
   135.31 LICENSED PRACTICAL NURSE (LPN)/PARAMEDIC.
   (a)   There are hereby established within the Division of Police two (2)
part-time positions of Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)/Paramedic for the
Corrections Facilities, who shall be under the control and supervision of the
Assistant Chief and the Facility Physician, to be appointed by the Mayor. The
position of Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)/Paramedic shall be within the
unclassified service.
   (b)   The Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)/Paramedic shall be responsible for
duties associated with providing inmate health services as are set forth in the
City’s Employee Job Descriptions and as the same are hereafter amended and
approved by the Mayor/Director of Public Safety, the Police Chief and Assistant
Chief.
   (c)   The Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)/Paramedic shall further perform
such duties on an on-call basis as required by the Assistant Chief.
   (d)   The Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)/Paramedic shall be at least
eighteen (18) years of age and a high school graduate or possess equivalent
experience and/or relevant education and hold a current Ohio license as a
Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) or shall be certified by the State of Ohio as a
Paramedic with a minimum of one (1) year LPN experience or Paramedic
experience.
   (e)   The Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)/ Paramedic shall be compensated in
a range starting at ten dollars ($10.00)/hr. to fourteen dollars ($14.00)/hr.
Raises shall be based on evaluation, attendance and merits, reviewed by the
Assistant Chief and reported to the Mayor. The Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN)/
Paramedic shall receive such benefits as indicated under Chapter
157, Employees Generally, for part-time employees.
(Ord. 2012-48. Passed 3-20-12.)
   135.32 FEES AND ANCILLARY COSTS FOR THE USE OF THE BEDFORD HEIGHTS POLICE
DEPARTMENT JAIL FACILITY.
   Regarding fees, ancillary costs and procedures for the use of the Bedford
Heights Police Department Jail Facility:
   (a)    The Bedford Heights Police Department Jail Facility ("Facility") may,
at the sole discretion of the Chief of Police or his designee, be used by
outside law enforcement agencies in a mutual aid status and be subject to the
following fees and ancillary costs for any prisoner so incarcerated:
      (1)    One hundred twenty-five dollars ($125.00) per day or any part of a
day for prisoner housing and services,
      (2)    One hundred percent (100%) of all medical, dental, vision,
psychological, or prescription medication costs or other health care expense,
and
      (3)    Full reimbursement for the hourly costs of any posted guard at an
outside medical facility for longer than two hours at the top overtime rate
under the current police collective bargaining unit agreement.
   (b)    Agencies requesting such mutual aid shall provide all transportation
to and from the Facility; shall provide all necessary information and
appropriate legal documentation justifying the incarceration including service
on the incarcerated defendant; and, shall pay all accumulated fees and costs
directly to the City of Bedford Heights as billed monthly.
   (c)    In the event that any incarcerated defendant requires transport to or
admission to a hospital or other medical facility, the involved agency will be
notified immediately and expected to take custody the prisoner at the Facility
within two hours, or arrange for the prisoner's legal release or furlough.
   (d)    The City of Bedford Heights may, at any time, and at its sole
discretion refuse to house prisoners due to available space, the medical or
psychological condition of any proposed prisoner, or for any other operational
reason including non-payment of past invoiced services.
   (e)    Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the ability of
the City of Bedford Heights to enter into mutually negotiated contracts for the
provision of jail services with or without different terms and as authorized by
the legislature.
      (Ord. 2024-088. Passed 11-6-24.)
   135.33 AUXILIARY POLICE.
   (a)   Appointment of Members. The Mayor is hereby authorized to commission a
number of men and women not to exceed a total of forty subject to the
discretion of the Mayor, as is necessary to supplement the regular police
force, which group shall be known as “Auxiliary Police Unit.”
(Ord. 2005-059. Passed 4-5-05.)
   (b)   Term of Service. Auxiliary police officers shall serve at the pleasure
of the Mayor, or until a resignation submitted by a member is accepted by the
Mayor.
   (c)   Qualification of Members. The members of the auxiliary police unit may
not be under the age of twenty-one years at the time of their appointment, and
shall meet such other requirements as provided by rules and regulations
provided for in subsection (e) hereof.
   (d)   Control of Unit.  The Mayor/Director of Public Safety shall be the
executive officer of the auxiliary police unit. The Chief of Police shall be
the commanding officer and shall have control of the assignment, training,
stationing and direction of work. The auxiliary police unit shall have only
such police powers and shall perform only such police duties assigned by the
Chief of Police in writing, such as writing certain parking tickets within the
City, and shall act only when in prescribed uniform or portion of uniform. The
Mayor/Director of Public Safety shall prescribe the time and place such
uniforms or portions thereof shall be worn. Such auxiliary members shall obey
the chain of command of the Division of Police and shall take official police
orders from all regular appointed members thereof.
   (e)   Rules and Regulations. The Mayor/Director of Public Safety shall
prescribe the rules and regulations for the organization, administration,
conduct and control of the auxiliary police unit.
   (f)   Uniform. The Mayor/Director of Public Safety is authorized to
prescribe by rules and regulations the type of uniform or part thereof which
shall be worn by members of the auxiliary police unit. All issued uniforms and
equipment will remain the property of the City of Bedford Heights and will be
returned to the City of Bedford Heights upon termination of employment. If
issued uniforms or equipment are damaged within the line of duty, the City of
Bedford Heights will repair or replace the damaged article. If issued uniforms
or equipment are damaged outside the course of duty, it will be the
responsibility of the auxiliary police officer to repair or replace the
article.
   (g)   Compensation.
      (1)   Auxiliary police officers shall serve as part-time employees and be
compensated for their services at the rate of nine dollars and fifty cents
($9.50) per hour, except as otherwise authorized by Council for services in the
municipal parks and for court appearances.
      (2)   Auxiliary police officers shall not be entitled to any part-time
employee benefits or any relief or pension funds of the City or the State of
Ohio, or any other similar benefit. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any
auxiliary police officer shall be entitled to any and all relief under Workers’
Compensation.
   (h)   Use of Uniform. No auxiliary police officer shall appear in public in
uniform unless scheduled or called to duty by the Police Chief or officer in
charge of the police department.
   (i)   Duty Assignments. During periods of emergency call-out auxiliary
police officers shall assist members of the police department by performing
whatever functions are necessary to protect life and property as may be
assigned by the police department shift officer. Auxiliary police officers may
work other non-emergency jobs only as approved and scheduled through the police
department. Auxiliary police officers shall not work in place of regular
officers of the City of Bedford Heights police department in non-emergency
situations.
   (j)   Auxiliary Liaison Officer. The Chief of Police may appoint a member of
the police division to be in charge of the auxiliary unit. This member of the
police department will be known as the Auxiliary Liaison Officer.
   (k)   Non-liability. This section is declared by Council as an exercise by
the City of its police powers for the protection of the public peace, health,
property, safety and general welfare. Neither the City, nor any agent or
representative of the City, an officer appointed under the provisions of this
section, or any individual, firm, partnership, corporation or the receiver,
trustee or any agent thereof, who in good faith executes any executive order,
rule or regulation promulgated pursuant to the provisions of this section,
shall be liable for injury or damage sustained to persons or property as the
direct proximate result of such action. In addition to any other
responsibilities or immunities, the members of the auxiliary police unit shall
bear the same responsibilities and the same immunities as any other regularly
employed member of the Division of Police, except as herein provided.
(Ord. 2004-199. Passed 12-21-04.)
   135.34 PHYSICAL PROFICIENCY.
   Effective January 1, 2004, the City and Union will develop a Physical
Proficiency Program that, if successfully passed by a commissioned police
employee, will result in an annual six hundred dollar ($600.00) allowance on
the following basis:
   (a)   The City and Union shall create a physical standards committee
comprised of at least two Union members and no less than one member of
management. This committee shall meet during working hours where practical and
shall not interfere in the regular duties of the department.
   (b)   This committee shall create the standards for the physical standards
test. Provided, however, that the City shall have the right to implement such
test after meeting and discussing with the union. This test shall have
reasonable standards based on those skills necessary for performance as a
police officer and must be applied in a fair manner.
   (c)   In order to be eligible for the allowance, the employee must qualify
no later than December 15 of the test year. Testing shall begin in August of
the year. If an employee fails the test, he/she shall have two additional
attempts to take the test. These attempts must be no less than two weeks apart.
Preparation of this test must be on non-work time and at the employee’s own
expense.
      (Ord. 2005-078. Passed 5-3-05.)
   135.35 POLICE DIVISION ADMINISTRATIVE AIDE.
   (a)   There is hereby established with the Division of Police the position
of full-time Administrative Aide who shall be under the control and supervision
of the Mayor/Director of Public Safety and the Chief of Police or his/her
designee. The Administrative Aide shall be appointed by the Mayor. Such
position shall be in the unclassified service of the City.
   (b)   The Police Division Administrative Aide shall work such hours and
shifts as are determined by the Chief of Police but shall work not less than
forty hours per week and shall perform such duties as are required by the Chief
of Police or his/her designee.
   (c)   The Police Division Administrative Aide shall be at least eighteen
(18) years of age and be a high school graduate or possess equivalent
experience and/or relevant education and shall perform such duties as set forth
in the City’s Employee Job Descriptions and as the same are hereafter amended
and approved the Mayor/Director of Public Safety and Police Chief.
   (d)   The Police Division Administrative Aide shall receive such
compensation as Council shall from time to time provide and such position shall
be in the unclassified service of the City and shall receive such benefits as
indicated under Chapter
157, Employees Generally, for full-time employees. (Ord. 2021-031. Passed 5-18-
21.)

   137.01 ESTABLISHMENT AND COMPOSITION.
   There is hereby established in and for the city a full-time Division of
Fire, to be manned by the number of firefighters hereinafter set forth who
shall be appointed by the Mayor and shall be in the classified service of the
city:
   (a)   One Fire Chief;
   (b)   One Assistant Fire Chief;
   (c)   Up to three Captains;
   (d)   Up to three Lieutenants;
   (e)   Firefighters in such number as Council from time to time shall
determine. For purposes of this section, the term “firefighters” shall include
the positions of Fire Chief, Assistant Fire Chief, Captains and Lieutenants.
      (Ord. 2012-36. Passed 3-6-12.)
   137.02 COMPENSATION AND BONDS.
   (a)   Members of the Division of Fire shall receive such compensation as
Council shall designate and shall post bonds for the faithful performance as
may be required by ordinance or resolution of Council.
   (b)   All members certified as an Emergency Medical Technician (E.M.T.)
shall be paid three hundred dollars ($300.00) on April 15 of each year.
   (c)   Except as indicated herein, employees not covered by a collective
bargaining agreement, including the Fire Chief and the Assistant Fire Chief,
shall receive such benefits as indicated under Chapter
157, Employees Generally.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.03 DUTIES.
   (a)   The Fire Chief shall perform the duties of his office as required by
law, shall at all times be available for call to duty in connection with such
office and shall be responsible to the Director of Public Safety.
   (b)   The Assistant Fire Chief shall perform such duties as are usually
performed by Assistant Fire Chiefs of fire departments and as the Fire Chief
shall order.
   (c)   The Captains shall be in charge of the shift, act as fire prevention
officer for business establishments within the City, and perform such duties as
are usually performed by Captains of fire departments and as the Fire Chief and
Assistant Fire Chief shall order.
   (d)   The Lieutenants shall be in charge of the shift in the absence of a
Captain and shall perform such duties as usually performed by Lieutenants of
fire departments and as the Fire Chief, Assistant Fire Chief and Captains shall
order.
   (e)   A fireman of the first grade shall first have served a probationary
period of one year, and one year as a second grade fireman, in the service of
the City, prior to becoming a fireman of the first grade. Such firemen shall
perform such duties as are usually performed by firemen of all grades and as
their superior officers shall order.
   (f)   The personnel of the Fire Department shall perform such specific
duties as are set forth in the City’s Employee Job Descriptions and as the same
are hereafter amended and approved by the Mayor and the Fire Chief.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.04 APPOINTMENTS.
   Appointments to any position in the Division of Fire shall be made by the
Mayor.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.05 TEMPORARY FIREMEN IN EMERGENCIES.
   In times of emergency, the Mayor may appoint additional personnel in the
capacity of special temporary firemen as he may deem necessary. Such
appointments, when made, shall be on a temporary basis, and persons so
appointed shall receive compensation only for the time actually devoted to fire
duties at the direction of the Mayor or the Fire Chief.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.06 APPOINTMENTS SUBJECT TO CIVIL SERVICE RULES; QUALIFICATIONS.
   (a)   All appointments to the Division of Fire, shall be subject to the
Rules and Regulations of the Civil Service Commission. All personnel in the
Fire Department shall be at least eighteen (18) years of age and be a high
school graduate or possess equivalent experience and/or relevant education.
(Ord. 2005-078. Passed 5-3-05.)
   (b)   It shall be a condition and qualification for examination and
appointment to the Division of Fire that any individual to be so appointed
after July 1, 1986, shall have fulfilled the requirements for certification as
an emergency medical technician paramedic by the State of Ohio. An applicant
may provide either State or National Certification as an emergency medical
technician paramedic at the time of filing an application to become a fire
fighter; provided, however, that proof of State Certification as an emergency
medical technician paramedic must be shown prior to an applicant being placed
on the eligibility list for the position of fire fighter.
   (c)   Those members presently within the Fire Department holding emergency
medical service or paramedic certificates shall continue to hold such
certificates and continue to be qualified to operate and work in emergency
medical service vehicles, in order to maintain a minimum of eight or more
qualified paramedics within the Fire Department at all times. Any present
paramedic may be exempt from continuing his or her certification due to health
or physical inability to perform paramedic services only upon application to
and approval by the Fire Chief.
   (d)   Unless a present member of the Fire Department is specifically
exempted by the Fire Chief, the loss of qualification of certification as a
paramedic shall be grounds for disciplinary action only after a hearing under
the Civil Service Rules by the Safety Director.
   (e)   The loss of qualification or certification as a paramedic prior to
appointment to the Fire Department shall be valid grounds for the non-
appointment of new personnel to the Fire Department or after appointment
grounds for disciplinary action and/or discharge only after a hearing under the
Civil Service Rules by the Safety Director.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.07 PHYSICAL EXAMINATIONS.
   (a)   All members of the Division of Fire, as a condition of employment upon
a job offer and before appointment to the Division, shall furnish written
evidence of physical and/or mental fitness for such position by submitting
themselves to a complete physical and/or psychological examination, at the
expense of the City, by a duly licensed physician to be chosen by the Mayor,
whose report shall be final.
   (b)   All employees of the Division of Fire shall submit to a physical
examination and complete stress test no more than once a year after their
appointment at the request of the Mayor or Fire Chief. This examination shall
only be related to the ability of the employee to perform his/her job. Each
employee shall authorize the physician to submit a written report of the
examination findings relative to the ability of the employee to perform his/her
job to the Fire Chief and/or the Mayor. If an employee is found to be unable to
perform his/her duty, the employee may elect to receive a second opinion from a
physician of his/her choice, at his/her own expense.
   (c)   All information obtained as a result of any physical and/or
psychological examination shall be kept as a confidential medical record and
put into separate files to be given out only under the conditions set forth at
Section
157.30.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.08 EXTENSION OF SERVICE AND EQUIPMENT TO OTHER MUNICIPALITIES.
    The Fire Chief is hereby authorized to extend the service of the Division
of Fire, or the use of its fire apparatus, to any other municipal subdivision
whenever, in his judgment and opinion, a sufficient emergency exists justifying
the need for such services or apparatus and the protection of the citizens and
property of this City will not be unduly jeopardized thereby.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.09 UNIFORM ALLOWANCE.
   (a)   Each member of the Division of Fire, regardless of rank, shall
receive, in addition to his regular compensation, an annual allowance toward
the purchase of regularly prescribed uniform and turnout clothing, including
blouse, trousers, cap, shirts to which insignia required by regulation are
permanently attached and cannot be ordinarily worn in civilian use as a result
thereof, dress uniform shoes, work shoes and fire boots, turnout coats,
helmets, sweatshirts, work trousers and coveralls. Such allowance shall be a
maximum of four hundred seventy-five dollars ($475.00) in any twelve-month
period, except that the maximum allowance for all new appointees during their
first year of service shall be in such amount as is approved by the Safety
Director to provide sufficient adequate uniforms and equipment. All such
uniforms shall be purchased by the employee who shall present to the Fire Chief
or his designee a proper receipt for such expenditures. The uniform allowance
shall be paid by check issued to the employee and distributed to the Fire Chief
or his designee in the amount of two hundred thirty-seven dollars and fifty
cents ($237.50) on April 15 and two hundred thirty-seven dollars and fifty
cents ($237.50) on October 15 of each year.
      (1)   Distribution of the checks shall be made by the Fire Chief or his
designee to the employees upon presentation to the Fire Chief or his designee
of the above-required receipts. The Chief or his designee shall collect all
such receipts and forward them to the Director of Finance.
      (2)   Each full-time member of the Division of Fire shall, in addition to
the above, receive an annual allowance of five hundred twenty-five dollars
($525.00) per year for cleaning of such uniforms. The maintenance allowance
shall be paid by check issued to the employee and distributed to the Fire Chief
or his designee in the amount of two hundred sixty-two dollars and fifty cents
($262.50) on April 15 and two hundred sixty-two dollars and fifty cents
($262.50) on October 15 of each year.
      (3)   Any Fire Fighter, incurring damage or destruction to any personal
fire equipment, clothing or gear, in the performance of his official duty,
shall be entitled to reimbursement from the City upon presentation of a claim
to the Fire Chief, with satisfactory proof thereof.
   (b)   All purchases of the uniform requirements of the Division of Fire
shall be in accordance with Chapter
153.
   (c)   Any uniforms or portions thereof paid for by the City shall be and
remain the property of the City during a member's probationary period in the
Division. However, upon receiving a permanent appointment to such Division such
articles of uniform clothing paid for by the City, shall thereafter become the
property of such member.
   Should an employee’s employment be terminated (voluntarily) within one (1)
year of the date of hire, the employee may be required to reimburse the City an
amount equal to the clothing allowance he received, or return all issued
uniforms and turnout equipment to the City.
   (d)   Such uniform allowances shall apply only to full-time members of the
Division.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.10 HIGH RISK SICK LEAVE.
   (a)   Whenever a full-time fire employee during the lawful performance of
assigned duties, including training, as a direct result of a “high risk”
situation or circumstance, suffers injuries causing total disability for more
than three full work days, “high risk” sick leave may be granted in lieu of
regular sick leave beginning with the fourth work day taken for sick leave
during such total disability, not to exceed ninety calendar days. If at the end
of such ninety day period the employee is still totally disabled and unable to
report for work, the “high risk” leave may, at the City’s sole discretion, be
extended for additional ninety calendar day periods. “High risk” sick leave
shall not be deducted from the employee’s accumulated sick leave account.
   (b)   “Total Disability” shall mean the physical inability of an employee to
perform regularly assigned duties at the station and/or otherwise engage in any
other gainful employment.
   (c)   In order to qualify for “high risk” sick leave, the following criteria
shall be certified by the Chief of the Division and approved by the Safety
Director and the Mayor:
      (1)   The injuries are the direct result of:
         A.   An accident occurring when lights and sirens are being used
pursuant to Division rules and regulations;
         B.   Falling objects;
         C.   Smoke or gas inhalation poisoning;
         D.   Bodily burns;
         E.   Falls during attempted rescue; or
         F.   Falls as a result of weakened structures in buildings.
      (2)   The illness is the direct result of or is caused by performing in
an emergency situation and results in contagious or infectious diseases
classified pursuant to Ohio R.C. 3701.24(B) which are contracted or as a direct
result of employment-related activities provided, however, the City retains the
right to determine, through separate medical examination, whether or not said
disease was employment related.
      (3)   The event herein described must be duly logged and a written report
submitted to the Chief’s office during the shift in which it occurs, or as soon
thereafter as practicable.
      (4)   Medical evidence has been provided within a reasonable period of
time (no more than fourteen days) from the employee’s treating physician and/or
the City physician establishing the cause, nature and extent of the injuries;
the likelihood of the term of disability; and the medical probability of full
recovery and eventual return to work.
      (5)   The City shall have the right at any time during the process to
request medical verification of the employee’s injury from his doctor. In
addition, the City shall have the right, at its expense, to send the employee
to a doctor of its own choosing for medical verification. In the event there is
a dispute between the employee’s physician and the City’s doctor, the parties
agree to send the employee to a third, neutral doctor, whose decision regarding
the process will be final.
         (Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.11 CONTRACT AUTHORIZED BY COUNCIL.
   Should any of the employees of the Division of Fire enter into an Agreement
authorized by Council concerning economic conditions and benefits, the terms of
the Agreement shall control the economic conditions and benefits of such
employees and any conflicting provision of this chapter shall be subject to the
terms of the Agreement for the covered employees.
(Ord. 2004-202. Passed 12-21-04.)
   137.12 ACCUMULATED SICK LEAVE.
   (a)   Effective January 1, 1998, a Fire Chief and Assistant Fire Chief with
ten (10) or more years of service who resigns, retires, is laid off or
dismissed, or upon death, the member or the member’s estate will be paid in
cash at the rate of one-half of his accumulated, but unused, sick leave credit
to a maximum benefit accrual of 3,300 sick leave hours. The maximum payment
(1,650 hours) will be based on the rate of pay at the time of retirement or
death. For purposes of compensation under this provision, hourly rate of pay
shall be defined as an employee’s actual base rate excluding all other wage
tied benefits.
   (b)   Effective June 1, 2010, the Fire Chief and/or Assistant Fire Chief
with fifteen (15) or more years of service in the Department of Fire shall be
entitled to withdraw pay from his/her accumulated sick time provided, however,
that such request for early withdrawal must be made in writing to the Director
of Finance at least sixty (60) days prior to the date requested for said
withdrawal on a form to be provided by the city. The reason for the request for
withdrawal must be to further the employee’s education or to pursue advanced
certifications related to the fields of firefighting and/or emergency medical
services and/or executive level management/leadership development education.
The eligible employee shall furnish proof satisfactory to the Finance Director
of application and registration for said course of study in the above-named
courses of study or courses related thereto prior to the withdrawal of said
funds. Early withdrawal of sick time shall be computed on the basis of the
employee’s hourly rate, based on his/her base pay, at time of approval. The
maximum withdrawal permitted shall be ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per year
by the eligible employee. The maximum amount an eligible employee may withdraw
under this provision is twenty thousand dollars ($20,000).
(Ord. 2010-057. Passed 5-4-10.)

   139.01 ESTABLISHMENT; DIRECTION AND CONTROL.
   (a)   There is hereby established the Division of Building, Engineering and
Inspection which shall be directed and controlled by a Building Official duly-
certified by the State of Ohio as required to meet the requirements for
certification as a Residential Building Department to enforce the Residential
Code of Ohio for One, Two, and Three-Family Dwellings as well as a
Nonresidential Building Department under Chapter 3781 of the Ohio Revised Code.
   (b)   He or she shall be appointed by the Mayor with confirmation of City
Council. He or she shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. Compensation for
said position shall be determined from time to time by Council.
   (c)   Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (b) above, the Mayor,
with the authorization and approval of Council, may contract for Building
Department services to provide the City with a duly-certified Building Official
and certified inspector so as to meet the requirements of the State of Ohio for
certification as a Residential Building Department necessary to enforce the
Residential Code of Ohio for One, Two and Three-Family Dwellings as well as a
Nonresidential Building Department under Chapter 3781 of the Ohio Revised Code.
   (d)   Whenever the term “Building Commissioner” is used in the Codified
Ordinances of the City of Bedford Heights, Ohio, said term shall also mean a
duly-certified “Building Official” who shall perform all the duties and have
all the powers of the “Building Commissioner” as outlined in the Codified
Ordinances. The terms Building Commissioner, Building Official and Zoning
Inspector shall be synonymous.
(Ord. 2012-134. Passed 7-17-12.)
   139.02 PERSONNEL.
   (a)   The individual and/or entity with which the City contracts for
Building Department Services shall provide the state-certified inspectors
required to enable the City to meet the requirements of a Residential Building
Department necessary to enforce the Residential Code of Ohio for One, Two and
Three-Family Dwellings as well as a Nonresidential Building Department under
Chapter 3781 of the Ohio Revised Code.
   (b)   The following additional personnel shall be appointed by the Mayor
under the immediate supervision of the Building Official. These personnel shall
receive the compensation as Council shall designate from time to time:
      (1)   Building Secretary (one);
      (2)   Full-Time Clerk/Secretary (one);
      (3)   Consulting Architect (one). (The Consulting Architect shall be a
registered architect to be employed as needed, at the discretion of the
Building Official and approval of the Mayor to inspect and review industrial,
commercial and apartment construction plans);
      (4)   Landscape Architect (one).
      (5)   Part-time Building Inspector (in-house) who shall possess all
current state certifications necessary to enforce all residential codes for
One, Two and Three-Family Dwellings including all applicable city, state and
federal codes.
(Ord. 2016-062. Passed 5-3-16.)
   139.03 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND DUTIES OF BUILDING DIVISION PERSONNEL.
   (a)    All personnel of the Division of Building, Engineering and Inspection
shall be at least eighteen (18) years of age and be a high school graduate or
possess equivalent experience and/or relevant education and shall perform such
duties as are set forth in the City’s Employee Job Description and as the same
are hereafter amended and approved by the Mayor and certified Building
Official.
   (b)   The Building Official shall hold and maintain a Class I Building
Official Certification and a valid Ohio driver’s license.
   (c)   All Building Code Inspectors and/or Part-time Inspectors charged with
the enforcement of all City, State and Federal Codes shall possess the required
certifications necessary to enforce all such codes. It shall be the
responsibility of the Building Official to monitor and insure that all Building
Code Inspectors and/or Part-time Inspectors hold the required current
certifications from the State of Ohio.
   (d)   The Building Secretary and full-time Clerk/Secretary shall perform
such duties as required by the Building Official.
   (e)   The Building Official or a Building Code Inspector shall be certified
as a Residential Building Official.
(Ord. 2012-134. Passed 7-17-12.)
   139.04 CITY ARCHITECT EMPLOYED.
   There shall be employed by the City a duly licensed Architect who shall
furnish to Council and the directors of all departments his professional advice
as hereinafter provided. He shall receive such compensation as authorized by
Council by ordinance.
(Ord. 2006-191. Passed 9-19-06.)
   139.05 ARCHITECT'S DUTIES.
   The City Architect shall:
   (a)    Give advice to Council, the Mayor and other proper administrative
officials on problems pertaining to architecture.
   (b)    Prepare formative or preliminary sketches, layouts, estimates,
reports or studies concerning the advisability of proceeding with any public
improvement contemplated by Council.
   (c)    Attend Council or committee meetings, conferences, etc., at the
request of the Mayor or Council.
   (d)    Upon request, make and deliver to the City monthly reports of the
progress of improvements under his charge, stating conditions of same, together
with any other matters or interest desired by the City. All plans shall be the
property of the Municipality and when so directed, be filed in the Clerk's
office upon completion of any improvement.
   (e)   The Architect's services shall be available to any department of this
Municipality and to any official acting in his official capacity in connection
with Municipal business.
      (Ord. 2006-191. Passed 9-19-06.)
   139.06 ADDITIONAL BUILDING FEES.
   (a)   The Building Commissioner is hereby authorized and directed,
commencing July 5, 1993, to collect and remit on behalf of the Board of
Building Standards an assessment equal to three percent (3%) of the prescribed
building permit fees as required by Senate Bill 359 and Ohio Administrative
Code 4101:2-1-50.
   (b)   The Building Commissioner is hereby authorized and directed,
commencing May 27, 2007, to collect and remit on behalf of the Board of
Building Standards an assessment equal to three percent (3%) of the prescribed
building permit fees for nonresidential buildings and one percent (1%) of the
prescribed building permit fees for residential buildings as required by House
Bill 175 and Section 3781.102(F) of the Ohio Revised Code and Ohio
Administrative Code 4101:8-1-03 103.2.4.2. (Ord. 2006-196. Passed 10-3-06.)
   139.07 LANDSCAPE ARCHITECT.
   There shall be employed by the City a duly licensed Landscape Architect to
furnish professional advice with respect to proposals for projects to be built
within the City, to provide necessary guidance for legislation with respect to
landscape proposals within the City and attend such meetings of the Planning
Commission or Architectural Board of Review as requested.
(Ord. 2006-191. Passed 9-19-06.)
   139.08 BACK-UP BUILDING CODE INSPECTOR.
   There is hereby established the position of Back-up Building Code Inspector
within the Division of Building, Engineering and Inspection, to be appointed by
the Mayor and to receive compensation of $25.00 per inspection. The Back-up
Building Code Inspector shall provide inspections only at times for which the
Building Code Inspectors are unavailable.
(Ord. 2006-191. Passed 9-19-06.)

   141.01 ESTABLISHMENT; SUPERVISION AND CONTROL.
   (a)   There is hereby established a Department of Community Life to be
organized and to perform such time as Council may from time to time provide
under the supervision and control of the Mayor.
   (b)   The Department of Community Life shall oversee all City-sponsored
community programs and diversity of programming for the purpose of recreation,
wellness, education, social support, senior citizens/disabled, cultural, arts
and general entertainment, and the operation of the municipal swimming pools
and grounds, the City parks and playgrounds and the community center and
outbuildings and ball diamonds.
   (c)   The Department of Community Life shall include the Division of Sports
& Leagues, the Division of Aquatics, the Division of Fitness, the Division of
Senior Citizen/Disabled, and the Division of Parks & Playgrounds.
   (d)   The Bedford Heights Community Life Department shall be committed to
educating and enlightening individuals and families by offering a wide range of
recreation and social opportunities essential to the health and well-being of
the community.
      (1)   Senior Citizen/Disabled Division. There is hereby established, in
the Department of Community Life, a division to be known as the Division of
Senior Citizens/Disabled whose mission shall be to administer programs to
assist Bedford Heights senior and disabled citizens age 62 and older.
      (2)   Sports & Leagues Division. There is established, in the Department
of Community Life, a division to be known as the Division of Sports and
Leagues, whose mission shall be to administer programs to provide sports and
sport-related activities, recreation and services.
      (3)   Aquatics Division. There is established, in the Department of
Community Life, a division to be known as the Aquatics Division whose mission
shall be to administer programs to provide aquatic facilities and services.
      (4)   Fitness Division. There is established, in the Department of
Community Life, a division to be known as the Division of Fitness, whose
mission shall be to administer programs to provide fitness facilities and
services.
      (5)   Parks & Playgrounds. There is established, in the Department of
Community Life, a division to be known as the Division of Parks & Playgrounds,
whose mission shall be to administer programs and operate park & playground
facilities owned by the City of Bedford Heights and located in the City of
Bedford Heights.
         (Ord. 2014-043. Passed 4-15-14.)
   141.011 DUTIES, RESPONSIBILITIES AND BENEFITS QUALIFICATION OF THE PERSONNEL
OF THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMUNITY LIFE.
   (a)   The duties and responsibilities of the personnel of the Department of
Community Life shall be set forth in the City’s Employee Job Descriptions and
as the same are hereafter amended and approved by the Mayor and the Director of
Community Life. Such employees (with the exception of Student Help) shall be at
least eighteen (18) years of age and a high school graduate or possess
equivalent experience and/or relevant education. Those employees not covered by
a collective bargaining agreement shall receive such benefits as indicated
under Chapter
157, Employees Generally.
(Ord. 2014-043. Passed 4-15-14.)
   141.02 DIRECTOR.
   (a)   The Director of Community Life (Full-Time), shall be appointed by the
Mayor and shall be supervised by the Mayor, shall be responsible for the
overall strategic and operational management and planning and budget of all
programs and activities of the Department of Community Life and municipal
swimming pools, the City parks, the playgrounds, the community center,
outbuildings and ball diamonds. The Director of Community Life shall supervise
all full- time and part-time staff members of the Department of Community Life
(with the exception of employees contracted by the City from other agencies).
The Director of Community Life shall also be responsible for all operations,
which includes marketing and promotion of the Community Center and Municipal
swimming pools, parks and playgrounds and all Department of Community Life
programs and activities. The Director of Community Life shall be responsible
for the supervision and management of all divisions of the Community Life
Department.
(Ord. 2014-043. Passed 4-15-14.)

2017-100.

   141.05 COMMUNITY LIFE MISCELLANEOUS REQUIREMENTS.
   (a)   Fees paid to the City for any pass or programs set forth above shall
not be refunded under any condition.
   
   (b)   Marketing Promotions. The Director of Community Life may recommend
adjustments to the above fees and giveaways for marketing promotions. As long
as they do not exceed the amount specified for advertising bids under Section
153.17, such promotions shall be approved by the Finance Director and Council
Community Life Committee.
(Ord. 2014-043. Passed 4-15-14.)
   (c)   Senior Citizen Grass-Cutting and Snow-Plowing Programs. Unless
otherwise indicated in this section, all participants in the senior citizen
grass-cutting and snow-plowing programs must have reached the age of 65 at the
time application is made for participation in said programs. Residents who have
established a disability pursuant to federal law may also participate in the
programs provided for in this subsection. Senior citizens who have reached the
age of 65 or are disabled as outlined above are disqualified from participation
in these programs if they reside in a household where there is an able-bodied
person who is capable of performing grass- cutting and snow removal tasks. This
section does not apply to any person who has reached the age of 62 and/or is
disabled and has previously participated in the above-described programs. These
services may be available on a “first-come, first-served” registration basis
only. Due to budgetary constraints, the City reserves the right to establish a
maximum number of participants in these programs.

participate in the senior-citizen grass-cutting program, shall pay an
application fee of thirty-five dollars ($35.00), which shall be used to help
defray the costs of said program.
      (2)   All eligible applicants, at the time of filing an application to
participate in the senior snow-plowing program, shall pay an application fee of
thirty-five dollars ($35.00), which shall be used to help defray the costs of
said program.
(Ord. 2016-024. Passed 2-2-16.)
      (3)   Council hereby authorizes the Mayor to allow for twenty-five (25)
additional emergency slots for citizens who miss the grass cutting and/or snow
plowing deadlines and to charge citizens an additional fee of thirty-five
dollars ($35.00) per program for a total fee of seventy dollars ($70.00).
         (Ord. 2024-026. Passed 4-16-24.)
 
   141.06 COMMUNITY LIFE AQUATICS MANAGER AND COMMUNITY LIFE SPORTS MANAGER.

for adults and youth.
   (d)   The Community Life Sports Manager shall possess the qualifications and

for this position prepared by the Mayor and Community Life Director.

   141.07 AQUATICS LIFEGUARDS AND INSTRUCTORS.

   (c)    There is hereby created the position of part-time Aquatics Instructor
who will be directly responsible to the Community Life Aquatics & Sports
Manager and who shall perform assigned aquatics instruction tasks as necessary
for operation of the outdoor municipal pool facility during the summer season
and aquatics instruction duties at the indoor municipal swimming pool facility
year-round as needed.

position prepared by the Mayor and Community Life Director.

Aquatics & Sports Manager and who shall possess the qualifications and perform
all job duties as indicated in the job description prepared by the Mayor and
Community Life Director.

(Ord. 95-034. Passed 2-7-95.)
   145.02 PROCEDURE; DUTIES; NOTICES.
   (a)    Meetings of the Planning Commission shall be held at the call of the
Chairman and at such other times as the Commission may determine or as required
by the City Charter or ordinances. All meetings of the Planning Commission
shall be open to the public.
   (b)    The Commission shall keep minutes of its proceedings, showing the
vote of each member upon each question or, if absent or failing to vote,
indicating such fact, and shall keep records of its examinations and other
official actions, all of which shall be immediately filed in the office of the
Commission, and shall be a public record.

Article X of the City Charter and ordinances.

reclassifications of the Planning and Zoning Code, notice of which shall be

which the proposed amendment, including text and maps, if any, may be examined
as required by Section
1135.03 of the Planning and Zoning Code. Notices shall be sent to all owners of
contiguous properties advising them of the time and date of any meeting where
the Planning Commission is to review antenna structure proposals and screening
plans and of their right to express their approval or disapproval of the same
at least fourteen days before the meeting as required by Section
1189.02(j) of the Planning and Zoning Code.
(Ord. 95-034. Passed 2-7-95.)
   145.03 QUORUM; DECISIONS.
   (a)    Four members of the Planning Commission shall constitute a quorum.
   (b)    A majority vote of those members present shall be required on all
matters coming before the Commission.
(Ord. 95-034. Passed 2-7-95.)
   145.04 APPLICATIONS; FEE.
   (a)   All applications shall be filed with the Planning Commission at least
seven days prior to its meetings with the exception of applications for antenna
structures which shall be filed with the Planning Commission at least fourteen
days prior to its meetings in order to provide the required notice in
accordance with Section
1189.02(j) of the Planning and Zoning Code and Preliminary Subdivision Plats
which shall be filed with the Planning Commission at least twenty days prior to
the meeting in accordance with Section
1103.02 of the Planning and Zoning Code.
   (b)   Each applicant shall accompany each application with a check made
payable to the City of Bedford Heights or a cash payment in the amount of one
hundred dollars ($100.00) to cover administrative costs for processing the
application.
(Ord. 2002-053. Passed 4-2-02.)
   145.05 COPIES OF PLATS AND PLANS.
   The original mylar and at least ten copies of all plats are to accompany all
applications to the Planning Commission for lot splits and consolidations and
subdivision plats. At least ten copies of all necessary plans are to accompany

other matters.
(Ord. 95-034. Passed 2-7-95.)
   145.06 FILING OF PLATS BY CITY.

(Ord. 95-034. Passed 2-7-95.)

CHAPTER 149
Disaster Services Agency
149.01    Creation; membership.
149.02    Appointment of Director; duties.
149.03    Functions.
149.04    Compensation.
CROSS REFERENCES
         Civil defense - see Ohio R.C. Ch. 5915
         Alternate seats of government in enemy attack - see Ohio R.C. 5915.041
   149.01 CREATION; MEMBERSHIP.
   There is hereby created a Disaster Services Agency for the City as an agency
of the government to prevent, minimize, repair and alleviate injury or damage
resulting from natural disaster or enemy attack. The Agency shall consist of a
Director and additional members to be appointed by the Director. All officers
and employees of the City are hereby declared to be members of the
organization, together with those volunteer forces appointed to aid them during
a disaster.
(Ord. 77-150. Passed 11-1-77.)
   149.02 APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTOR; DUTIES.
   The Director of the Disaster Services Agency shall be appointed by the
Mayor, subject to the confirmation of Council, and shall serve at the pleasure
of the Mayor. The Director shall coordinate the organization, administration,
planning and operations of all local agencies for civil defense and disaster
services subject to the direction and control of the Mayor as provided by
statute.
(Ord. 77-150. Passed 11-1-77.)
   149.03 FUNCTIONS.
   The Disaster Services Agency shall perform such functions within the
Municipality as are prescribed in and authorized by Ohio R.C. Chapter 5915 and
the Governor's regulations promulgated thereunder, and in addition shall
perform such duties outside the corporate limits as are required pursuant to
mutual aid arrangements with any other political subdivision or with the
countywide civil defense or disaster services organizations. In performing
duties pursuant to this chapter, the Disaster Services Director shall cooperate
with other political subdivisions, with countywide civil defense or disaster
service organizations; with the State and with the Federal government, through
appropriate channels, and with private agencies in all matters pertaining to
the civil defense or disaster service activities of the City.
(Ord. 77-150. Passed 11-1-77.)
   149.04 COMPENSATION.
   The Director and other disaster service personnel appointed or assigned as
herein provided may receive such compensation as may be provided for by Council
from time to time.
(Ord. 77-150. Passed 11-1-77.)
